claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
claims.statement: The authors hypothesize that airway spheroids keep cilia in the lumen because basal cells interact with the surrounding high-viscosity matrix, and that moving spheroids to a lower-viscosity, water-based medium may trigger basal cells to migrate inward so the ciliated apical layer takes their place on the spheroid surfa

claims.title: Apical-in spheroids become motile within a week in low-adhesive liquid culture
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
claims.statement: Human bronchial epithelial spheroids that are apical-in and non-motile on release from Matrigel become motile by day 7 in low-adhesive liquid culture, with beating cilia on their outer surface; immunostaining shows a large increase in external multiciliated cells between day 0 and day 7.

claims.title: Higher culture viscosity reduces Anthrobot motility and size
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
claims.statement: Culturing Anthrobots in environments more viscous than the protocol baseline decreases both their motility and their size, suggesting that low-viscosity environments favour the growth of functional, larger bots.

claims.title: Initial cell seeding density is a control knob for Anthrobot size and maturation
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
claims.statement: Changing the initial seeding density of bronchial epithelial cells in Matrigel (half, default or double 30,000 cells/mL) significantly changes the resulting Anthrobot sizes and the time course of motility, though not linearly, suggesting that seeding density is a tractable control parameter for Anthrobot morphology and

claims.title: Anthrobot motility onset follows a sigmoidal time course peaking around day 10
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
claims.statement: After release from the matrix, the number of motile Anthrobots rises along a sigmoidal curve over three weeks, with the largest change in motility on day 10, and this rise reflects a morphological reorganization that exposes cilia on the surface.

claims.title: Anthrobot motility is cilia-driven
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
claims.statement: Blocking ciliary motion with ciliobrevin sharply decreases Anthrobot motility, showing that their locomotion is driven by surface cilia.

claims.title: Anthrobot trajectories fall into four movement types
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types
claims.statement: Unsupervised clustering of 30-second trajectory segments from about 200 Anthrobots, described by straightness and gyration indices, yields four statistically distinct movement types: circular, linear, curvilinear and eclectic.

claims.title: Circular motion is the most stable Anthrobot behaviour; eclectic motion is transient
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types
claims.statement: In a Markov-chain model of transitions between movement types, circular motion is the most persistent Anthrobot behaviour, followed by linear and curvilinear motion, while eclectic motion acts as a transient intermediate that probabilistically resolves into one of the other three types.

claims.title: Anthrobots self-organize into discrete, stable movement types with individual fingerprints
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types
claims.statement: Because Anthrobot movement types are highly consistent and rarely interconvert (for example between circular and linear), the authors conclude that Anthrobots self-organize into discrete, stable movement types, each bot having a distinct motility fingerprint.

claims.title: Morphotype 2 is most ciliated; morphotype 3 has the most polarized cilia
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Distinct Morphological Types
claims.statement: Among the three Anthrobot morphotypes, morphotype 2 (the largest and least regular) is significantly more ciliated than the other two, and morphotype 3 has a significantly more polarized, clustered cilia distribution with the fewest isolated cilia patches.

claims.title: Anthrobots form three morphotypes, split first by size and shape, then by cilia pattern
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Distinct Morphological Types
claims.statement: Principal component analysis and clustering of eight shape and cilia indices from about 350 Anthrobots yields three morphotypes, organized as a decision tree in which size and shape smoothness separate small, smooth spherical bots (morphotype 1) from larger, irregular bots, which are then split by cilia pattern into no

claims.title: Non-movers, linear and circular bots map onto morphotypes 1, 2 and 3
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Distinct Movement Types and Morphotypes are Highly Correlated
claims.statement: Anthrobot behaviour and morphology are significantly associated: non-moving bots fall mostly in morphotype 1 (small, smooth, spherical), linear movers mostly in morphotype 2 (large, non-polarized cilia) and circular movers mostly in morphotype 3 (polarized cilia), and no displacing bot was found in morphotype 1.

claims.title: Spherical bots with uniform cilia may not move because ciliary forces cancel
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Distinct Movement Types and Morphotypes are Highly Correlated
claims.statement: Morphotype 1 Anthrobots are likely non-movers or stationary wigglers, which the authors suggest may be because their radially symmetric spherical shape with evenly distributed cilia makes ciliary propulsion forces cancel out, with small imbalances producing only wiggling.

claims.title: Linear-moving Anthrobots are more bilaterally symmetric about their movement axis
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis
claims.statement: Linear-moving Anthrobots show higher bilateral symmetry of cilia distribution about their axis of movement than circular movers; for circular bots, but not linear bots, the 90-degree rotated axis is more symmetric than the movement axis (p = 0.048), supporting distinct local symmetry profiles for distinct movement type

claims.title: Anthrobots recapitulate the bilateral symmetry of many wild-type species
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis
claims.statement: The link between straight-line movement and bilateral symmetry in Anthrobots suggests that these synthetic forms, self-assembling in a symmetrical environment, recapitulate a fundamental morphological property seen in many wild-type species and could be used to study how embryos establish a single body midplane.

claims.title: Faster and more rotational Anthrobots cover more of a neuronal scratch
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro
claims.statement: Anthrobots can move across scratches in human neuronal monolayers in vitro, and bots with higher rotational tendency or higher speed cover a larger proportion of unique positions along the scratch interface.

claims.title: An intermediate gyration maximizes how closely Anthrobots track scratch edges
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro
claims.statement: In a constrained set of 13 Anthrobots in neuronal scratches, gyration (rotational tendency) has a quadratic relationship with how closely a bot's trajectory follows the scratch edge (p = 0.006), suggesting an intermediate gyration range maximizes edge tracking.

claims.title: Superbot bridges induce neuronal gap closure in scratched monolayers
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues
claims.statement: Fused Anthrobot assemblies (superbots) placed across a scratch in a human neuronal monolayer induce substantial regrowth of neuronal tissue beneath them within 72 hours, forming a stitch that connects the two sides of the scratch.

claims.title: Superbot-induced gap closure is local and restores native tissue density
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues
claims.statement: Neuronal gap closure occurs only at the site where a superbot is placed; the neuronal coverage density there is statistically indistinguishable from intact tissue outside the scratch, while adjacent and distant parts of the scratch have significantly lower coverage.

claims.title: Passive mechanical loading does not reproduce Anthrobot-induced neural repair
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues
claims.statement: Placing a piece of agarose on neuronal scratches for 4 days to provide passive mechanical loading induces no repair, indicating that simple mechanical contact is not sufficient for the gap closure seen with Anthrobot superbots.

claims.title: Anthrobots and Xenobots share similar movement types and transition profiles
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion
claims.statement: Anthrobots and Xenobots both show discrete movement types with very low interconversion between linear and circular motion (0.2% and 0.3% for Anthrobots, 0.5% and 1.6% for Xenobots) and highly consistent circular behaviour (92% and 95%), though Anthrobot linear behaviour is more consistent (80% versus 67%).

claims.title: Similar forms from divergent genomes point to generic laws of morphogenesis
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion
claims.statement: Because Anthrobots and Xenobots, despite highly divergent genomes, ages and tissue origins, assemble into very similar kinds of motile constructs, the authors conclude that generic laws of morphogenesis matter in addition to species-specific genomic information.

claims.title: Superbot size is set by bot number and fusion requires exposed basal layers
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion
claims.statement: Anthrobots fuse into larger superbots only in the days immediately after release from the matrix, while their basal layers are still exposed and can mediate bot-to-bot fusion, and superbot size can be controlled by the number of Anthrobots cultured together in a well.

claims.title: Tracheal cells healing neural tissue could not be predicted from current models
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion
claims.statement: That wild-type cells from the trachea move over and heal neural tissue is unexpected given their normal role in the body and could not be predicted from any current molecular or tissue-level model, which suggests screening engineered tissue interactions to uncover novel cell capabilities.

claims.title: Patient-derived Anthrobots could be deployed in vivo without an immune response
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion
claims.statement: Because Anthrobots are made from adult human tissue, they could in future be personalized for each patient and deployed in that patient's body without triggering an immune response.

claims.title: Anthrobots may be made from other ciliated human cells such as oviduct or ependyma
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Conclusion
claims.statement: Anthrobots may be generable from other ciliated human cells, such as oviductal epithelium or brain ependymal cells, and non-ciliated cell types could be used for bots that need no autonomous motility.

claims.title: One genome yielding diverse forms in different environments could shape evolution
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Conclusion
claims.statement: The additional morphogenetic competencies revealed by Anthrobots could matter for evolutionary developmental biology, since the evolution of anatomical and functional features could be affected by the ability of the same genome to produce very diverse forms in different environments.

claims.title: A collective's perceptual field and ability to find alternative paths grow with its size
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction
claims.statement: Extending William James' definition of intelligence (reaching the same goal by different means) to collectives via the perceptual field, the region of space and time an agent can survey for alternative paths to a goal, the authors propose that as a collective grows its perceptual field increases, improving its ability

claims.title: Neural unification into a self is a pivot of earlier morphogenetic cell communication
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction
claims.statement: It has been hypothesized, and the authors adopt, that the ability of neurons to unify into a centralized self is an evolutionary pivot of earlier cell-communication strategies that first solved problems in anatomical morphospace, a domain also requiring information processing above the single-cell level.

claims.title: The number of embryos a blastoderm forms is not fixed by genetics
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Development: transition to multicellularity
claims.statement: The number of individuals formed by an embryonic blastoderm is not fixed at one by the genome: temporarily introducing breaks that informationally isolate islands of cells yields twins, triplets and so on, showing the blastoderm is an excitable medium in which several coherent embryos can self-organize.

claims.title: Keratocyte fragments migrate to the anode while whole keratocytes migrate to the cathode
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Cell migration: the group does not go where each of the parts wants to go
claims.statement: In an electric field, whole keratocytes migrate toward the cathode while fragments of keratocytes migrate toward the anode, so the collective (an intact cell) has the opposite taxis to its parts, illustrating that collective behaviour can be a hard-to-predict function of component tendencies.

claims.title: Targeting instructor-cell voltage converts tadpole melanocytes to a melanoma-like state
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › From normal melanocytes to a melanoma phenotype: a collective decision
claims.statement: In Xenopus tadpoles, briefly targeting the bioelectric state of a small population of instructor cells (with a chloride channel activator or a GlyCl mutant), in the absence of carcinogens, oncogenes or DNA damage, converts melanocytes throughout the animal, including distant ones, into an over-proliferative, invasive m

claims.title: Melanocyte conversion is all-or-none per animal, stochastic only across the cohort
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › From normal melanocytes to a melanoma phenotype: a collective decision
claims.statement: Melanocyte conversion after instructor-cell depolarization is a collective, all-or-none decision: different reagents give different incidences in a cohort (e.g. 70% converted), but each animal is either fully converted or fully normal; a computational model fitted to these incidences predicted interventions (two drugs

claims.title: Head-versus-tail choice at a planarian cut cannot be made locally
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions
claims.statement: When a planarian is cut once, cells that were adjacent neighbours at the same positional-information value make a head on one side and a tail on the other, so this anatomical decision cannot be made locally: wound cells must coordinate with the rest of the fragment to learn where they are, which way they face and what

claims.title: Cryptic planaria randomize head number per animal, not per cell
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions
claims.statement: Perturbing the planarian bioelectric control circuit produces 'Cryptic' destabilized worms whose fragments, even from the same parent, regenerate one-headed and two-headed forms at a set frequency of about 1:2, yet each animal has clear heads and tails rather than mixed tissue, so the randomized bioelectric state is in

claims.title: Left-right randomization is concordant within an embryo except after VANGL knockdown
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions
claims.statement: Bioelectric and biochemical perturbations of vertebrate left-right patterning randomize laterality only at the level of whole embryos (each embryo's cells agree on L and R identity); the only known perturbation that breaks this concordance is down-regulation of planar-polarity VANGL signalling, which produces speckled

claims.title: Grafted groups of neural crest cells keep their identity; single grafted cells do not
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Neural crest intelligence is collective
claims.statement: Single neural crest cells transposed to a different anterior-posterior axial domain change their gene expression to match their neighbours, whereas groups of transposed cells keep their original gene expression, which the authors interpret as collectives having greater positional memory (a perceptual field extending fu

claims.title: The segmentation clock needs a cell collective to oscillate and entrains grafted cells
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Segmentation intelligence is collective
claims.statement: The vertebrate segmentation clock depends on collectivity: presomitic mesoderm cells do not oscillate when cultured individually but resume oscillating when cultured together, wild-type cells grafted into non-cycling mutant fish express her1 without cycling, and cells grafted into tissue at a different clock phase sync

claims.title: Frog embryo brain gene expression is driven by voltage differences, not absolute values
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Conclusion
claims.statement: In the frog embryo brain, downstream gene expression is driven by the spatial difference in membrane voltage between regions rather than the absolute voltage of any cells, so cells must read patterns over whole cell fields: collectivity appears in the input as well as the output of cell-group behaviour.

claims.title: Biological memory preserves salience rather than fidelity
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › Abstract
claims.statement: Levin proposes that memory, across scales from cells to societies, is best understood as preserving salience (what matters for the agent's future) rather than fidelity to the details of the original data.

claims.title: Adaptive confabulation resolves the persistence paradox for individuals and lineages
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › Abstract
claims.statement: Levin argues that the paradox that a changing agent or species ceases to be itself while an unchanging one dies out is resolved by continuous commitment to creative, adaptive confabulation (reinterpretation of memories and information) at levels from molecular to behavioural, in individuals and whole lineages.

claims.title: Memories may be active agents in the sense-making process
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › Abstract
claims.statement: Levin speculates that, on a substrate-independent, processual view of life and mind, memories, as patterns in the excitable medium of cognitive systems, could be seen as minimally agential participants that help shape their own reinterpretation, blurring the line between thoughts and thinkers.

claims.title: Reinterpreting non-local memories is a cognitive glue that makes Selves
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 1. Introduction and Overview
claims.statement: Levin proposes that mnemonic improvisation, the ability to modify, remap and interpret non-local memories onto new media and contexts, is one of the kinds of cognitive glue that binds parts into a Self at every scale.

claims.title: Memories surviving metamorphosis are remapped to stay salient in the new body
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 3. Remapping Memories: Beyond Storage and Simple Modification
claims.statement: In insects whose memories survive metamorphosis (caterpillar to butterfly), recall does not carry over specific caterpillar memories but generalizes and remaps them (e.g. from leaves to food) so that the learned relationship keeps its salience in the new body and environment.

claims.title: Engrams act more like prompts decoded by an intelligent receiver than like encodings
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 3. Remapping Memories: Beyond Storage and Simple Modification
claims.statement: From examples such as frogs that seek out an odorant injected into the egg they developed from, Levin argues that engrams behave less like encoded memories and more like prompts, with much of the work (detecting novelty, remapping across scales, contextualizing and generalizing) done by the encoding and decoding proces

claims.title: The same bioelectric trigger is reinterpreted by context (monensin: tails vs legs)
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere
claims.statement: Low-information bioelectric triggers are interpreted by competent tissues according to context: the voltage-modifying reagent monensin induces tail regrowth in tadpoles but leg regrowth in froglets, never the reverse, preserving high-level information such as 'build whatever normally goes at this location'.

claims.title: Polyploid newts build normal tubules by switching molecular mechanisms
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere
claims.statement: Engineered polyploid newts with much larger cells keep kidney tubule diameter normal by using fewer cells and, with truly enormous cells, a single cell bending around itself, showing that tissues call up different molecular mechanisms (cytoskeletal bending instead of cell–cell communication) to reach the same anatomica

claims.title: Bowtie compression is common in biochemical, bioelectric and mechanical pathways
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere
claims.statement: Levin argues that a bowtie architecture, which compresses data to a generative kernel that must later be re-inflated and reinterpreted, is common at the subcellular scale in biochemical, bioelectrical and biomechanical pathways, as well as in the egg stage of the metazoan life cycle and in learning.

claims.title: Anatomical plasticity across species reflects willingness to confabulate in morphospace
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere
claims.statement: Levin proposes that the spectrum from hardwired, mosaic C. elegans through intermediately plastic amphibians and embryonic mammals to extremely plastic planaria reflects a strategic parameter: the willingness to confabulate in anatomical space, i.e. to rely on pattern extraction and completion rather than taking geneti

claims.title: Planaria resist cancer and ageing despite noisy genomes via pattern completion
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere
claims.statement: In silico simulations show how lineages such as planarian flatworms can become extremely resistant to transgenesis, ageing, cancer and injury despite very noisy genomes because they commit to a strategy that overrides genetic details with large-scale pattern completion.

claims.title: Substrate unreliability is the reason, not an obstacle, for biological intelligence
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development
claims.statement: Levin argues that the noise and unreliability of biological matter is a feature rather than a bug: morphological and behavioural intelligence arose because of, not in spite of, the vulnerability of the substrate, as suggested by planaria having the noisiest genome and the best regeneration and cancer resistance.

claims.title: Cellular competency hides genome quality from selection, driving an intelligence ratchet
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development
claims.statement: Because competent biological material compensates for defects, selection cannot see genome quality clearly, so more evolutionary change accrues in competency mechanisms than in structural components, producing a positive-feedback intelligence ratchet based on remapping information to new contexts.

claims.title: There is no single substrate for memory; all components can serve as scratchpads
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development
claims.statement: Levin hypothesizes that there is no single substrate for memory: every component of a living system can use everything in its environment, including the high-dimensional reservoir of subcellular structure, as an interpretable scratchpad, rather than engrams residing only in synapses.

claims.title: Training associative memories may increase integration of composite systems
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 7. A Continuum: From Thoughts to Thinkers
claims.statement: Levin proposes that memories belonging to a collective (e.g. a rat's lever–reward association, which no single cell experiences) may help reify the collective Self, and that training associative memories into gene regulatory networks should be tested for increases in integrated information (self-coherence).

claims.title: Consciousness may be palpated uncertainty about one's own memories
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 7. A Continuum: From Thoughts to Thinkers
claims.statement: Extending Solms's idea that consciousness is palpated uncertainty about the outside world, Levin hypothesizes that consciousness is palpated uncertainty about one's own memories and internal states.

claims.title: Behavioural intelligence evolved from morphogenetic problem-solving
claims.chapter: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 8. Conclusions
claims.statement: Levin proposes that behavioural intelligence in 3D space evolved from morphogenetic problem-solving competencies in anatomical space, which were themselves required by the inevitability of mutation and injury.

claims.title: Planaria have chaotic genomes yet regenerate, resist cancer and do not age
claims.chapter: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Introduction
claims.statement: Planaria, despite chaotic mixoploid genomes from ~400 million years of asexual reproduction and large numbers of plastic proliferative stem cells, are champions of regeneration, cancer resistant and apparently do not age, the opposite of what a 'genome drives function' paradigm would predict.

claims.title: The body is a collective intelligence, so behavioural tools should beat micromanagement
claims.chapter: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Introduction › BOX 1
claims.statement: Levin's central hypothesis is that the body is a collective intelligence behaving in anatomical, physiological and transcriptional spaces, so behavioural-science tools developed to collaborate with complex systems should provide therapeutic advantages over biochemical micromanagement of molecular components.

claims.title: Intelligence is reaching the same goal by different means, including in morphogenesis
claims.chapter: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Intelligence Below the Cellular Level
claims.statement: Levin defines intelligence, following William James, as the ability to reach the same goal by different means; for tissues this is the problem-solving competency to adapt to conditions in order to construct and repair a specific morphology or function, a functional definition that lets intelligence be studied in non-ne

claims.title: Gene regulatory network models show habituation, sensitization and Pavlovian learning
claims.chapter: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Intelligence Below the Cellular Level › The Inner Life of Active Matter
claims.statement: When standard behavioural-training protocols are applied to even simple models of gene regulatory networks and molecular pathways, the models show habituation, sensitization and Pavlovian (associative) conditioning, a dynamical state memory that requires no change to network topology or edge strengths.

claims.title: Planarian heads degenerated by barium regenerate adapted to it via a handful of genes
claims.chapter: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Intelligence Below the Cellular Level › The Inner Life of Active Matter
claims.statement: Planarian flatworms exposed to barium, a nonspecific potassium channel blocker, lose their heads but soon regenerate new heads completely adapted to barium, and transcriptomic analysis shows only a handful of genes up- or down-regulated, which Levin interprets as cells solving a problem in high-dimensional transcriptio

claims.title: Morphogenesis is behaviour of cell collectives navigating anatomical morphospace
claims.chapter: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › The Collective Intelligence of Cell Groups › Morphogenesis as Behavior in Anatomical Space
claims.statement: Morphogenesis can be viewed as behaviour in anatomical morphospace: cellular collectives actively navigate from various starting states to the region corresponding to the species-specific target morphology, with competency ranging from a constrained random walk to advanced problem-solving, a framing Levin presents as a

claims.title: Anatomical homeostasis uses large-scale feedback loops that reduce error from a target

claims.statement: Applied systemically, the same bioelectric-modifying drug (monensin) triggers tail regeneration at tail wounds and leg regeneration at leg wounds, showing that the specificity of the regenerative response lies in the responding cell collective rather than in the reagent.

claims.statement: Levin proposes that aging is due to the degradation of endogenous bioelectric pattern memories required throughout life to maintain tissue order, so that solutions to aging need to target this information scaffold as well as cell-level rejuvenation (e.g. Yamanaka factors).

claims.title: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)
claims.chapter: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)
claims.statement: The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.

claims.title: Fisher-KPP wave of advance of an advantageous gene
claims.chapter: The wave of advance of advantageous genes (1937)
claims.statement: An advantageous allele spreading through a continuous population advances as a travelling wave whose speed is set by the selection coefficient and the diffusion (dispersal) rate.

claims.title: Fisher's principle of equal investment in the sexes
claims.chapter: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)
claims.statement: Under random mating and autosomal inheritance, selection drives parents to invest equally in sons and daughters, which gives a 1:1 sex ratio when the two cost the same.

claims.title: Fisher's infinitesimal model of quantitative inheritance
claims.chapter: The Correlation between Relatives on the Supposition of Mendelian Inheritance (1919)
claims.statement: Continuous traits determined by many Mendelian loci of small additive effect produce the observed correlations between relatives, so biometric and Mendelian inheritance are consistent.

claims.title: Turing diffusion-driven instability
claims.chapter: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)
claims.statement: A homogeneous steady state of two reacting chemicals that is stable without diffusion can become unstable to spatial perturbations when the chemicals diffuse at different rates, spontaneously producing a pattern.

claims.title: Turing wavelength selection
claims.chapter: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)
claims.statement: The spacing of a Turing pattern at onset is set by the reaction rates and diffusivities, not by the size of the tissue, so changing these parameters predictably changes the number of repeated elements.

claims.title: Reaction-diffusion of morphogens accounts for biological pattern
claims.chapter: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)
claims.statement: Chemical substances that react and diffuse through tissue (morphogens) are sufficient to account for the main phenomena of morphogenesis.

claims.title: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele
claims.chapter: On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population (1962)
claims.statement: The probability that a mutant allele eventually fixes in a finite population depends on its initial frequency, its selective advantage and the effective population size, and equals its initial frequency when it is neutral.

claims.title: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate
claims.chapter: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level (1968)
claims.statement: For neutral mutations the long-run rate of molecular substitution equals the mutation rate per generation, independent of population size, which yields a molecular clock.

claims.title: Mean time to fixation of a neutral mutant
claims.chapter: The average number of generations until fixation of a mutant gene in a finite population (1969)
claims.statement: A neutral mutant that does go to fixation takes on average about four times the effective population size, in generations, to do so.

claims.title: Neutral equilibrium heterozygosity (Kimura-Crow)
claims.chapter: The number of alleles that can be maintained in a finite population (1964)
claims.statement: Under neutral mutation to new alleles and drift, expected heterozygosity reaches an equilibrium that rises with the product of effective population size and mutation rate.

claims.title: Neutral theory: most molecular substitutions are neutral
claims.chapter: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level (1968)
claims.statement: Most evolutionary changes at the molecular level are caused by random drift of selectively neutral or nearly neutral mutations, not by positive selection.

claims.title: Hamilton's rule
claims.chapter: The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I (1964)
claims.statement: A gene for social behaviour increases in frequency when the benefit to the recipient, weighted by genetic relatedness, exceeds the cost to the actor.

claims.title: Haplodiploidy hypothesis for eusociality
claims.chapter: The genetical evolution of social behaviour. II (1964)
claims.statement: Because full sisters in haplodiploid species share three quarters of their genes, more than a mother shares with her offspring, haplodiploid insects are predisposed to evolve sterile worker castes.

claims.title: Local mate competition sex ratio
claims.chapter: Extraordinary Sex Ratios (1967)
claims.statement: When a few mothers lay eggs on a patch and their offspring mate there before the daughters disperse, the evolutionarily stable sex ratio is female-biased, and the bias weakens as the number of mothers grows.

claims.title: Declining force of selection with age
claims.chapter: The moulding of senescence by natural selection (1966)
claims.statement: The strength of selection on survival falls with age after reproduction begins, so senescence is an inevitable outcome of natural selection.

claims.title: Evolutionarily stable strategy conditions
claims.chapter: The Logic of Animal Conflict (1973)
claims.statement: A strategy is evolutionarily stable if, once common, it cannot be invaded by any rare alternative strategy.

claims.title: Hawk-Dove mixed ESS
claims.chapter: Evolution and the Theory of Games (1982)
claims.statement: When the cost of injury exceeds the value of the contested resource, the stable outcome is a mixture in which animals escalate with probability equal to the ratio of resource value to injury cost.

claims.title: War of attrition ESS
claims.chapter: The theory of games and the evolution of animal conflicts (1974)
claims.statement: In contests settled by display, where the animal willing to persist longer wins and costs grow with time, the stable strategy is to choose a persistence time at random from an exponential distribution whose mean equals the resource value.

claims.title: Twofold cost of sex
claims.chapter: The Evolution of Sex (1978)
claims.statement: An asexual mutant female in a sexual population with equal sex ratio produces twice as many grandchildren as a sexual female, so sex needs a compensating advantage of up to twofold to persist.

claims.title: Genetic hitchhiking (selective sweep)
claims.chapter: The hitch-hiking effect of a favourable gene (1974)
claims.statement: When a favourable mutation sweeps to fixation, it reduces genetic variation at closely linked neutral sites, and the reduction is larger the tighter the linkage relative to the strength of selection.

problems.q: Which explicit genetic projection and fixed-average-effect assumptions give a faithful Lean target for this extracted Fisher record?
problems.was: The finite Price identity and a conditional Hamilton regression corollary have compiled. Total fitness variance is not generally additive genetic variance.
problems.bio: Specify the genetic projection and partial-change operation against primary sources before any prover run.
problems.math: Independent statement-fidelity review, exact target freeze, compiled projection/covariance correspondence, standard axiom audit and controls that distinguish total from additive variance.
problems.title: Connect the Price identity to Fisher's additive-genetic partial change

problems.q: For one specified biological system, what measured and modeled quantities are needed to evaluate a transport claim?
problems.was: A protein structure prediction alone does not provide binding affinity, turnover or effective tissue diffusivity.
problems.bio: Choose a matched assay and audit the measured quantities before proposing a BioNeMo computation.
problems.math: A source-linked dataset with matching biological context, explicit transport/kinetic model, held-out calibration and a stated remaining uncertainty or documented insufficiency of evidence.
problems.title: Determine what evidence could connect molecular predictions to tissue transport

problems.q: Within a frozen kinetics/domain/initial-condition ensemble, where do linear predictions and converged nonlinear outcomes differ?
problems.was: An admissible growing linear mode and a finite-time nonlinear pattern are different observables. Solver nonconvergence must remain visible.
problems.bio: Align the existing runner's observables and convergence categories before interpreting its movies or aggregates.
problems.math: Preregistered observables, amplitudes, horizons and tolerances; independent linear calculation; numerical convergence checks; unresolved cases reported; no universal biological threshold claim.
problems.title: Separate linear instability from the nonlinear pattern a simulation produces

problems.q: Which source-to-record mappings preserve the mathematical object, quantifiers, units and scope?
problems.was: The 21-record audit checks hashes and copied fields. It does not establish faithfulness to original papers. Several records already state conditions that a short headline hides.
problems.bio: Begin with Fisher and Hamilton, then release independent source-review shards for the remaining records.
problems.math: Pinned source and passages, reviewed mapping of statement/math/context, explicit disagreements and versioned corrections. Citation presence alone is insufficient.
problems.title: Check that extracted claims preserve their source's actual meaning

problems.q: Can a second participant inspect and reuse a scoped contribution to change a different research action?
problems.was: Local self-tests and a coordination message do not demonstrate external reuse. Mycelium and other systems already provide close coordination precedents.
problems.bio: Agree the Delphi contribution format and offer one small replay or source-review task to an existing participant.
problems.math: Attributable second-participant run, exact consumed contribution version, applicability check, resulting artifact, independent review and measured overhead/cost.
problems.title: Demonstrate one independent, useful reuse across participants

problems.q: Which allocation rule improves accepted contributions or useful downstream decisions per constrained resource without starving exploration and replication?
problems.was: Votes, agent count and post volume do not establish scientific progress. Agent-economy proposals already discuss resource and credit allocation.
problems.bio: Define the decision-maker's objective, acceptance predicates and resource constraints before choosing a voting or market mechanism.
problems.math: Pinned task pool, separate interest/resource/blocking signals, preregistered utility and costs, expert-order and simple allocation baselines, coverage and failed/negative work included.
problems.title: Test whether attention and resource allocation improve useful progress

problems.q: Which admissible perturbations preserve the declared bridge volume?
problems.was: The n=1 sine displacement has nonzero integral and violates the stated fixed-volume constraint; independent review caught the benchmark interpretation before its agent evaluation.
problems.bio: Reuse this review as a regression check when future benchmarks define admissible modes.
problems.math: Exact integral witness and primary-source correspondence under the stated fixed-volume interpretation, recorded in the linked review.
problems.title: Reject the volume-changing mode in the pinned liquid-bridge benchmark
